rv.q: Director Evan Cabnet has aimed at, and struck, the tender heart in a script that could easily be performed with more darkness or more cartoony.
The big pleasure comes from watching true comic artists spin this trite material into gold.
But the money shot of this production is an incandescent comic turn by Ari Graynor, her inventive line readings matched by the daffy expressivity of her face and body.
Most of the jokes from the new Broadway comedy 'The Performers' cannot appear in a family newspaper.

There must be a way to say this without sounding prim. "The Performers," which finds a game but miscast Henry Winkler and a sweet Alicia Silverstone in Vegas at the Awards, is not shocking because of the nonstop use of playground dirty words or because of its unblinking attitude toward it...
For it soon becomes clear that “The Performers” is going to the planet of second-tier sitcoms.

The Performers is basically a delivery mechanism for flaccid double entendres, trumped-up sitcom couple squabbles, and soupy makeups; it makes absolutely nothing of its thrilling, frightening, topsy-bottomsy backdrop.
At Broadway prices, this greeting-card wisdom doesn’t come cheap.
The Performers is everything the masses want on Broadway: It's short (just 90 minutes), sexy (a send-up of the porn industry), and ruled by a ditzy scene-stealer.
It is undoubtedly a crowd-pleasing show, combining raunchy humor with a simple setup and conservative emphasis on monogamy.
But despite the chuckles, The Performers tended to remind me of one of the satirical porn titles mentioned in it: I Ate Chinese and Now I'm Hungry Again.
Some are amusing, but those who are more discriminating about penis and masturbation jokes may find the barrage of hit-or-miss material tedious after a while.
Everyone in the limp comedy hails from the planet Stupid.
I had a similar emotion at 'The Performers,' which opened Wednesday night at the Longacre Theatre.
I can come up with no other excuse for the presence of David West Read’s purported comedy about the adult-film industry, “The Performers,” at the Longacre Theatre.

cn.t: Raunchy porn-industry comedy draws mixed reviews for its crude language and thin plot, though critics praise Ari Graynor's standout performance. Most find it surprisingly sentimental beneath the vulgarity, but ultimately too sitcom-like and insubstantial.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
